rēgīna, rēgīnae f.

noun, first declension · Declension on Wiktionary

A queen in her own right, as Cleopatra, or a king’s wife (Lewis & Short). In comedy also a fine lady, against the maids (Plaut., Ter.), and in the poets a king’s daughter (see princess). Also the queen in cards and in chess (Traupman 51–52).

Examples

  • īnfandum, rēgīna, jubēs renovāre dolōrem

    too deep for words, my queen, is the grief you bid me live againVerg. A. 2.3

See also king, princess, prince, palace.
